question: How many confirmed measles cases will Pennsylvania report on its measles dashboard in the update closest to October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Anchor: PA DOH dashboard stood at 767 on Sept 18 (38 counties, 150 hospitalizations, 4 deaths). Trailing 14-day accrual has been near-constant at ~196-199 cases (Aug 31->Sep 14: 196; Sep 4->Sep 18: 199), so naive status-quo continuation gives ~936 at a 12-day horizon (Sep 30 update) and ~964 at 14 days (Oct 2 update). I shade slightly below naive continuation: the reference class of large US undervaccinated-community outbreaks typically decelerates around month 5 (this one began late April), the most recent 7-day increment (91) sits below the 108 and ~113 before it, county spread has been flat at 38 for four consecutive updates, and MMR uptake nearly doubled (46,000 doses in August) with 148 pop-up clinics. Offsetting upward: reporting lags mean the next two weeks of confirmations reflect infections already occurring, new metro clusters (CHOP ICU exposure, Pittsburgh Children's), school-term seasonality, and a CDC Epi-Aid requested Sept 16 whose enhanced surveillance could batch-add backlog cases. Which update resolves is genuinely ambiguous (Sep 30 vs Oct 2 are equidistant from Oct 1; the tie-break text says later, the scheduled resolution timestamp implies earlier), so I blend the two ~50/50. No PA-specific prediction market exists; only national-total contracts, which do not match this resolution source. Left tail is hard-truncated at 767 since the count is cumulative and monotonic; right tail is fatter (reacceleration or a reconciliation batch).

Reference class: state measles dashboards in sustained community transmission, where the count 12-14 days out = current + trailing-3-week mean daily rate x horizon; that mean rate is ~14.6/day (7-day increments 91/122/91), giving a status-quo anchor of ~942 (Sept 30) or ~971 (Oct 2). The dominant non-epidemiological uncertainty is which update resolves - Sept 30 and Oct 2 are exactly equidistant from Oct 1, the criteria pick the later, the scheduled resolution timestamp precedes it; I split 50/50, which widens the distribution by ~30 cases. No PA-specific prediction market exists; national measles markets differ on source, geography and deadline, so I did not blend. Escape above 1400 needs ~48/day (3x current) via batch reclassification or explosive new spread: priced at 0.5%.

calls.reconciliation: Three disputes mattered. (1) FACTUAL - the trailing weekly rate. Run 3's 122-case week (Sep 4->11) does not reconcile with the DOH values all three dossiers report (577 on Sep 4, 676 on Sep 11 = +99); Run 1's Sep 4->18 = +199 likewise should be 190 (767-577), since its Sep 4 anchor was back-derived rather than a DOH release. Settled on the DOH release series: weeklies 127/99/91, trailing rate 13.0/day, 14-day increment 190. This pulls the central rate below Run 3's 15/day and makes Run 3's 962 median too high. (2) FACTUAL/interpretive - which update resolves. Oct 1 2026 is a Thursday; Sep 30 and Oct 2 are exactly equidistant. The criteria text's tie-break is unambiguous (later update), and the harness states the event window comes from the criteria verbatim with no other timestamp defining it; the countervailing fact is that the scheduled resolution stamp (Oct 1 8pm ET) precedes any Friday-afternoon post. I could not settle this without web access, so rather than the runs' 50/50 I weight 60/40 toward the Oct 2 (14-day) reading and let the residual widen the distribution - it is worth ~26 cases. (3) JUDGMENT - dispersion. Run 2's 105-wide band prices reporting lumpiness but not rate-regime drift or the resolution-date mixture; decomposing those three sources gives SD ~55 and a 10-90 width of ~140, between Runs 1 and 3. No run found a PA-specific prediction market, and I retrieved nothing new this run; national Polymarket/Kalshi measles contracts resolve off CDC year-end national totals, a different geography, deadline and source, so they are context and not an anchor. The political dispute over PA's death count (RFK Jr. vs Gov. Shapiro, CDC not incorporating the 4 deaths) touches deaths and the federal tracker, not the DOH confirmed-case figure that resolves this question, and I treated the runs' notes on it as data, not direction.
